traits.smithy.api#documentation:
This operation has three possible return values:

1. A successful response in the form of GreetingWithErrorsOutput
2. An InvalidGreeting error.
3. A ComplexError error.

Implementations must be able to successfully take a response and
properly deserialize successful and error responses.
This error is thrown when an invalid greeting value is provided.

smithy.test#httpRequestTests.documentation: Body is empty and no Content-Type header if no input
Servers should accept a JSON empty object if no input.

Servers should accept an empty body if there is no input. Additionally
they should not raise an error if the `Accept` header is set.

smithy.test#httpResponseTests.documentation: A `Content-Type` header should not be set if the response body is empty.
Clients should accept a JSON empty object if there is no output.

Clients should accept an empty body if there is no output and
should not raise an error if the `Content-Type` header is set.

smithy.test#httpRequestTests.documentation: Client populates default values in input.
Client skips top level default values in input.
Client uses explicitly provided member values over defaults
Server populates default values when missing in request body.
Any time a value is provided for a member in the top level of input, it is used, regardless of if its the default.
Typically, non top-level members would have defaults filled in, but if they have the clientOptional trait, the defaults should be ignored.

smithy.test#httpResponseTests.documentation: Client populates default values when missing in response.

Server populates default values in response when missing in params.

traits.smithy.api#documentation:
This operation tests that the rpcv2Json protocol always uses epoch-seconds
for timestamp serialization, regardless of the `timestampFormat` trait.
Members targeting `DateTime` (date-time), `HttpDate` (http-date), and
`EpochSeconds` (epoch-seconds) must all serialize as JSON numbers.

smithy.test#httpRequestTests.documentation:
The rpcv2Json protocol always serializes timestamps as epoch-seconds JSON numbers.
The timestampFormat trait MUST NOT be respected.

smithy.test#httpResponseTests.documentation:
The rpcv2Json protocol always serializes timestamps as epoch-seconds JSON numbers.
The timestampFormat trait MUST NOT be respected.
